subject: Esther
note: Written in one pass from FIGURE-BRIEF.md. Every Bible line quotes the BSB (shared/bsb-berean-standard-bible.txt); the Greek additions quote the World English Bible (shared/web-world-english-bible.txt, book code ESG, whose chapter-and-verse numbers match ebible.org/eng-web/ESG04.htm). Every quotation is in esther.quotes.json and passes verify-quotes.mjs. Fetched texts are in sources/people/esther/ (gitignored).

life.text: Mordecai, a Benjaminite in the citadel of Susa, brought up Hadassah, that is Esther, the daughter of his uncle, because she had no father or mother; he took her as his own daughter.

Vashti refused to come at the king's command and was put away; a search for young women followed; Esther was taken to the palace under Hegai, kept her people secret at Mordecai's word, had twelve months of beauty treatments (six with oil of myrrh, six with perfumes), asked for nothing but what Hegai advised, and was crowned in the seventh year of Xerxes.
Mordecai learned of the plot of Bigthan and Teresh and told Esther, who told the king on his behalf; the men were hanged and it was written in the chronicles.

Haman the Agagite, raised above the princes, sought to destroy all the Jews because Mordecai would not bow; the Pur was cast in the twelfth year, the day fell on 13 Adar; Haman offered ten thousand talents of silver; the letters ordered the Jews destroyed.
Mordecai's warning ('for such a time as this') and Esther's answer: a three-day fast, night or day, and 'if I perish, I perish'. She had not been called to the king for thirty days.
The king held out the gold scepter; three times he offered her 'even up to half the kingdom' (5:3, 5:6, 7:2); twice she asked only for a banquet (5:4, 5:8).

The sleepless night, the chronicles read, Mordecai honoured, Haman made to lead him through the city square; the second banquet, Esther names Haman, who is hanged on the fifty-cubit gallows he built for Mordecai.
Esther receives Haman's estate, reveals Mordecai, weeps at the king's feet; the new letters let the Jews defend themselves; Mordecai in royal robes of blue and white; letters to the 127 provinces.
life.source: Esther 8 (BSB); 1:1 and 9:30 for the 127 provinces 'from India to Cush'.

life.text: 13 Adar; Esther asks for a second day in Susa and the hanging of the bodies of Haman's ten sons; Purim on 14 and 15 Adar; Queen Esther wrote 'with full authority', and 'Esther's decree confirmed these regulations about Purim' (the last the Bible tells of her).
God and the LORD are never named in the Hebrew (Protestant) book of Esther.
life.source: Checked: no line of Esther in the BSB contains the word God or LORD (grep, 0 hits in 167 verses). The Greek text (WEB, ESG) names God 24 times and the Lord 23 times in this translation.

life.text: The Greek additions, with the prayers of Mordecai and Esther (ESG 4:18-47 in the WEB), her fainting before the king (ESG 5:1-2) and Mordecai's dream, are in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles; Jerome placed them at the end of his Latin translation; the Council of Trent declared them canonical.
life.source: Catholic Encyclopedia (1909), 'Esther'; Jewish Encyclopedia, 'Esther, Apocryphal Book of' (sources/people/esther/je-esther-apocryphal.txt).

life.text: Name: Hadassah, 'myrtle'; Esther from the Persian 'stara' (star) according to some, or Ishtar according to others. The CE says 'From the Hebrew meaning star, happiness'.
life.source: Esther 2:7; Jewish Encyclopedia 'Esther'; Catholic Encyclopedia 'Esther'; LSB commemoration biography for 24 May ('Her Jewish name was Hadassah, which means "myrtle."').

life.text: Her family had been deported from Jerusalem; the CE identifies Assuerus with Xerxes (485-465 BC); the Greek text and Josephus call the king Artaxerxes; Sulpicius Severus 'I confess that I cannot easily perceive with what kings especially I should connect the actions of their lives'.
life.source: Catholic Encyclopedia 'Esther'; Greek Esther (WEB) uses Ahasuerus in its English but the LXX and Josephus read Artaxerxes (Josephus, Antiquities 11.6.1: 'his son Cyrus, whom the Greeks called Artaxerxes'); Sulpicius, Sacred History 2.12 (shared/npnf211.txt).

life.text: Jewish tradition places her tomb at Hamadan (Ecbatana), beside Mordecai's; the Fathers took Esther as a type of the Virgin Mary.
life.source: Catholic Encyclopedia 'Esther': 'Jewish traditions place the tomb of Esther at Hamadân (Ecbatana). The Fathers of the Church considered Esther as a type of the Blessed Virgin Mary.' Jewish Encyclopedia 'Esther', picture caption 'Traditional Tomb of Esther and Mordecai'.

life.text: The rabbis: one of the four most beautiful women ever created; counted among the prophetesses of Israel.
Purim custom: Haman's name written on the soles of shoes and stamped on, and rattles, at the reading of the Megillah.
Josephus calls Mordecai her uncle ('she was brought up with her uncle Mordecai'); the Hebrew says 'the daughter of his uncle' (a cousin); Sulpicius says 'cousin-german'.
life.source: Josephus, Antiquities 11.6.2 (Whiston); Esther 2:7 (BSB); Sulpicius, Sacred History 2.12.

fathers.text: Clement of Rome, 1 Clement 55: 'Esther also, being perfect in faith, exposed herself to no less danger...' (ANF 1, Roberts-Donaldson; New Advent prints Keith's ANF 9 translation, which reads 'who sees', so the cite points to CCEL's ANF 1).
Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy 3.21.123: 'Why did Queen Esther expose herself to death...'. Also Letter 63.29 'Esther by her fasts moved a proud king' (not used on the page).

John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Statues 3.6 (Antioch, 387, while Bishop Flavian went to Theodosius): 'There was a certain Hebrew woman, Esther was her name...' He goes on to quote her Greek prayer as a model for Flavian.
fathers.source: shared/npnf109.txt; the same words at New Advent 190103.

fathers.text: Josephus, Antiquities 11.6.10: 'But God laughed to scorn the wicked expectations of Haman; ... for that night he took away the king's sleep'. Also 11.6.2: the young women 'were in number four hundred' (not used on the page after trimming).

feasts.text: Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod: Esther, 24 May, with a short biography.

OCA: 'the righteous Esther, who delivered Israel from death' is named on the Sunday before the Nativity (18 to 24 December). She is not among the OCA's separate lives for the Sunday of the Forefathers (checked the list for 14 December 2025).

No day for her in the 1916 Roman Martyrology, the 1969 Calendarium Romanum, the Church of England calendar or Lesser Feasts and Fasts 2022 (only a passing mention under Argula von Grumbach). The Catholic Mass reads her Greek prayer (Esther C:12, 14-16, 23-25) on Thursday of the First Week of Lent.

could_not_verify: That Esther is the only book of the Hebrew Bible missing from the Dead Sea Scrolls: a good tidbit, but Britannica refused the fetch and no public-domain source was at hand. Left out.

Luther's Table Talk remark that he wished the book did not exist: the Catholic Encyclopedia reports it (Table Talk, 59), but the Gutenberg Table Talk (Hazlitt) does not carry it. Left out rather than quote Luther through a Catholic polemic.
Jerome's own preface to Esther is not in NPNF 2-6 as printed by New Advent; what he did with the additions is told from the Catholic Encyclopedia only (not on the page).
The date of Lastman's painting (often given as 1618) is not on Commons or Wikidata: printed as 'early 1600s'.

checker_2026_09_25.checked: One light pass. Read the page whole. Checked: the LSB calendar for 24 May (and its line 'God intervenes on behalf of his people'); the OCA's 'The righteous Esther, who delivered Israel from death' (Sunday before the Nativity); the 1916 Martyrology (no Esther); the Catholic Encyclopedia (tomb at Hamadan, the Fathers' type of the Virgin); the Jewish Encyclopedia ('one of the four most beautiful women ever created', 'counted among the prophetesses', the names on the soles of shoes, the tomb picture of Esther and Mordecai); Sulpicius, Sacred History 2.12 (he cannot easily tell which Artaxerxes); Chrysostom, Statues 3 (her method was supplication, so 'prayer' is fair); Josephus's 'uncle'; the three offers of half the kingdom (5:3, 5:6, 7:2). Licences: all four Commons files match the page. The hub card is centred with the eyes at about 38%.
changed: The first moment said 'Then Queen Vashti refused', as though it followed Esther's upbringing; Vashti's refusal comes first (chapter 1). It now reads 'Before this, Queen Vashti had refused ... The king had put her away, and now he sent out a search'.
Greek Esther 4:31: 'You alone are our King' (a title for God, capitalised like 'O King of gods' in her prayer).
left_for_owner: The two gallery paintings both show her leaning back in distress (the writer's note); Lastman can go if it feels repetitive.
